result.title: ChainFlow: Few-Step Latent Flow Matching for Speculative Decoding
result.summary: Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate LLM inference: a lightweight drafter proposes tokens that the target verifies in one parallel pass. Existing drafters face trade-offs that limits their speedups: autoregressive drafters generate tokens one at a time, so drafting cost grows with draft length, while diffusion drafters generate tokens in parallel but predict each position independently, ignoring inter-token dependencies. We introduce ChainFlow, a new speculative decoding paradigm and the first flow-matching drafter conditioned on the target's hidden states. ChainFlow treats drafting as a short transport over hidden states, needing one or two flow steps instead of the many denoising steps of generation from noise. A variational autoencoder compresses these states so drafting cost barely grows with target size, lightweight feedback heads restore inter-token dependencies, and tree drafting raises acceptance. On Qwen3.5 models, at matched drafter size and training data, ChainFlow outperforms EAGLE-3 and DFlash in vLLM by 39% and 11%, respectively. These gains further widen as drafters are adapted to new languages sequentially. Our ablations cover drafter design and concurrent serving, and we open-source our code and drafter models.

AI.brief_summary: ChainFlow 将 speculative decoding 的草稿生成视为隐状态空间上的短程 flow matching 传输，仅用一到两步即可从目标模型隐状态产生候选 token，并用 VAE 压缩隐状态、轻量反馈头恢复 token 间依赖，配合树式草稿提升接受率。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文以少步 flow 在隐状态上做并行状态更新并用反馈头补回序列依赖，可为 LVR 中「如何并行生成或更新 latent 推理状态、并以少步传输替代多步去噪」提供方法线索，但其研究对象是纯文本 LLM 的草稿加速、无视觉证据筛选，需核查隐状态传输是否保留任务必要信息。
